items.title: Step 1
items.description:
In this workshop, you will leverage JavaScript to build a roster of astronauts for a space mission. 

To begin, create an empty array for your roster named `squad`.

hints.text: You should create a `squad` variable.
hints.test: assert.isDefined(squad);

hints.text: Your `squad` variable should be an array.
hints.test: assert.isArray(squad);

hints.text: Your `squad` array should be empty.
hints.test: assert.deepEqual(squad, []);

items.title: Step 2
items.description:
Your roster begins with a single commander astronaut. Create an object named `firstAstronaut` with the following properties:

| Key | Value |
| ----------- | ------- |
|`id`|`1`|
|`name`|`"Andy"`|
|`role`|`"Commander"`|
|`isEVAEligible`|`true`|
|`priority`|`3`|

hints.text: You should create a `firstAstronaut` variable.
hints.test: assert.isDefined(firstAstronaut);

hints.text: Your `firstAstronaut` should be an object.
hints.test: assert.isObject(firstAstronaut);

hints.text: Your `firstAstronaut` object should include the correct property values.
hints.test: assert.deepEqual(firstAstronaut, { id: 1, name: "Andy", role: "Commander", isEVAEligible: true, priority: 3 });

items.seed: const squad = [];

items.title: Step 3
items.description: Mission control requires a method for adding new members to the roster. Create an empty function named `addCrewMember` that accepts two parameters, `crew` and `astronaut`.

hints.text: You should create a function named `addCrewMember`.
hints.test:
const explorer = await __helpers.Explorer(code);
assert.exists(explorer.allFunctions.addCrewMember);

hints.text: Your `addCrewMember` function should have parameters `crew` and `astronaut`.

items.title: Step 4

hints.text: Your function should use a `for` loop to scan existing `crew` members (any valid `for (...)` form is fine).
hints.test: assert.match(__helpers.removeJSComments(code), /for\s*\([^)]*\)/);

hints.text: Inside the `for` loop, you should check for a duplicate `id`. If one is found, log `"Duplicate ID: " + astronaut.id"` to the console and then call `return` to exit the function.
When given valid inputs, your `addCrewMember` function should not invoke a `console.log()` error message or an early `return` exit.

items.title: Step 5
items.description: Push the `astronaut` object into the `crew` array and log `Added ${astronaut.name} as ${astronaut.role}` to the console. You can use either template literals or string concatenation for the log message.

hints.text: You should push the `astronaut` into the `crew` array.
You should log the astronaut's `name` in the following format, `Added {astronaut.name} as {astronaut.role}`.

items.title: Step 6
items.description: Now you can start building your roster. Use `addCrewMember()` to add the `firstAstronaut` to your `squad`.

hints.text: You should call `addCrewMember()` with `squad` and `firstAstronaut`.

items.title: Step 7
items.description:
The rest of your crew has been created in an array named `remainingCrew` with the following data: 

| id | name | role | isEVAEligible | priority |
| -- | ---- | ---- | ------------- | -------- |
|`2`|`"Bart"`|`"Pilot"`|`false`|`8`|
|`3`|`"Caroline"`|`"Engineer"`|`true`|`4`|
|`4`|`"Diego"`|`"Scientist"`|`false`|`1`|
|`5`|`"Elise"`|`"Medic"`|`true`|`7`|
|`6`|`"Felix"`|`"Navigator"`|`true`|`6`|
|`7`|`"Gertrude"`|`"Communications"`|`false`|`4`|
|`8`|`"Hank"`|`"Mechanic"`|`true`|`2`|
|`9`|`"Irene"`|`"Specialist"`|`true`|`5`|
|`10`|`"Joan"`|`"Technician"`|`false`|`1`|

Loop through the `remainingCrew` array and add each astronaut to `squad` using the `addCrewMember()` function.

hints.text: You should use a `for` loop to call `addCrewMember()` with each astronaut in `remainingCrew`.

items.title: Step 8
items.description: You had previously added a `console.log()` call to your `addCrewMember` function to validate its behavior, and now the call is no longer needed. To prevent the terminal from getting cluttered in future steps, go ahead and remove the current `console.log()` call.

hints.text: Remove the `console.log()` call from your `addCrewMember` function. You should delete the entire line.

items.title: Step 9
items.description:
Mission control needs a method to swap the positions of two crew members in a roster. Create an empty function named `swapCrewMembers` with three parameters:

- `crew`: an array of astronaut objects

- `fromIndex`: the index of the first astronaut to swap 

- `toIndex`: the index of the second astronaut to swap

hints.text: You should create a function named `swapCrewMembers`.
hints.test:
const explorer = await __helpers.Explorer(code);
assert.exists(explorer.allFunctions.swapCrewMembers);

hints.text: Your `swapCrewMembers` function should have parameters `crew`, `fromIndex`, and `toIndex`.

items.title: Step 10
items.description:
As before, start by validating the input inside the `swapCrewMembers` function. Specifically, you must validate the indices of the astronauts to be swapped. 

If any of the following are true: 

- `fromIndex` is negative

- `fromIndex` is greater than or equal to `crew.length`

- `toIndex` is negative

- `toIndex` is greater than or equal to `crew.length`

then, you should log `"Invalid crew indices"` to the console and call `return` to exit the function.

You can use the OR operator `||` to check multiple conditions at once:

```js
if (condition1 || condition2 || condition3 || condition4) {
  console.log("Message");
  return;
}
```

hints.text: You should validate indices using an `if` statement.
You should first validate indices and, if invalid, log the message `"Invalid crew indices"` before exiting the function using `return`.
Immediately after logging the message in the validation check, invoke `return` to exit the function early.
When given valid inputs, your `swapCrewMembers` function should not log any error messages and should not exit early.

items.title: Step 11
items.description:
You should create a shallow copy of the `crew` array using the `slice()` method. Name the new array `updatedCrew`.

Recall that calling `slice()` without arguments returns a copy of the entire array:

```js
const copyArray = originalArray.slice();
```

hints.text: You should use the `slice()` method to copy the input `crew` array and store the result in a new variable named `updatedCrew`.

items.title: Step 12

hints.text: You should perform the swap by calling the `splice()` method.
hints.test: assert.match(swapCrewMembers.toString(), /splice\s*\(/);

hints.text: You should call `splice()` with the `updatedCrew` array to perform the swap. You should use the one-line technique.
Your `swapCrewMembers` function should not mutate the original input `crew` array.

items.title: Step 13
items.description: Use a `for` loop to log the `name` of every astronaut in the `updatedCrew` array. After the loop, return the `updatedCrew` array to complete your `swapCrewMembers` function.

hints.text: You should use a `for` loop to iterate through the `updatedCrew` array and log the `name` of each astronaut.
You should return the `updatedCrew` array after logging its astronauts' names.

items.title: Step 14
items.description: Mission control has requested you to swap the positions of two astronauts in your `squad` array, specifically members at indices `2` and `5`. Use your `swapCrewMembers()` function to perform the swap and store the result in a new variable named `updatedSquad`.

hints.text: You should use `swapCrewMembers()` to swap `squad` members at indices `2` and `5` and store the resulting array in a new variable named `updatedSquad`.

items.description: You had previously added a `console.log()` call to your `swapCrewMembers` function to validate its behavior, and now the call is no longer needed. To prevent the terminal from getting cluttered in future steps, go ahead and remove the current `for` loop that logs to the console.

items.title: Step 16
items.description: Mission control requires a method for copying EVA-eligible astronauts from a crew. Create an empty function named `getEVAReadyCrew` that accepts a `crew` parameter.

hints.text: You should create a function named `getEVAReadyCrew`.
hints.test:
const explorer = await __helpers.Explorer(code);
assert.exists(explorer.allFunctions.getEVAReadyCrew);

hints.text: Your `getEVAReadyCrew` function should have a `crew` parameter.

items.title: Step 17
items.description: First, create an empty array named `eligible`. Then loop through every astronaut in the input `crew` array and, if they are EVA-eligible (meaning their `isEVAEligible` property is `true`), push them into the `eligible` array. After the loop, return the `eligible` array.

hints.text: You should create an empty array named `eligible`.
You should use a `for` loop to iterate through the input `crew` array.
hints.test:
const cleaned = __helpers.removeWhiteSpace(__helpers.removeJSComments(getEVAReadyCrew.toString()));
assert.match(cleaned, /for\s*\(/);

hints.text: You should return the `eligible` array.
After calling `getEVAReadyCrew()`, the returned array should contain only EVA-eligible astronauts from the input array `crew`.

items.title: Step 18

hints.text: You should have a function named `sortByPriorityDescending` with a `crew` parameter.
Your `sortByPriorityDescending` function should use two nested `for` loops to perform the sort.
hints.test:
const loopMatches = sortByPriorityDescending.toString().match(/for\s*\(/g) || [];
assert.isAtLeast(loopMatches.length, 2);

hints.text: Your `sortByPriorityDescending` function should sort the input `crew` by `priority` in descending order.
Your `sortByPriorityDescending` function should directly sort the input `crew` array in-place and not return a new array.

items.title: Step 19
items.description: Back inside the `getEVAReadyCrew` function, call `sortByPriorityDescending()` with the local `eligible` array so that it is sorted before being returned.

hints.text: You should call `sortByPriorityDescending()` with the local `eligible` array.

items.title: Step 22
items.description: Mission control has requested a new function for breaking down a crew into chunks of variable sizes. Create an empty function named `chunkCrew` that accepts two parameters, `crew` and `size`.

hints.text: You should create a function named `chunkCrew`.
hints.test:
const explorer = await __helpers.Explorer(code);
assert.exists(explorer.allFunctions.chunkCrew);

hints.text: Your `chunkCrew` function should have `crew` and `size` parameters.

items.title: Step 23
items.description: As before, you should validate your input. Specifically, if `size` is less than `1`, you should log `"Chunk size must be >= 1"` to the console and then call `return` to exit the function.

hints.text: If the input `size` is invalid, you should log the following error message to the console, `"Chunk size must be >= 1"`.
After logging the error message, you should immediately call `return` to exit the function early.
Your `chunkCrew` function should pass validation without errors when `size` is greater than or equal to 1.

items.title: Step 24
items.description:
To create chunks of size `n` from an `array` without changing it, you can combine a `for` loop with the `slice()` method as such: 

```js
const result = [];
for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i += n) {
  result.push(array.slice(i, i + n));
}
```

The example above:

- creates an empty array named `result`

- loops through the original `array` in steps of size `n`

- creates chunks from `array` of size `n` and pushes them into `result` using `slice()`

To complete the `chunkCrew` function, you must: 

- create an array named `chunks`

- loop through `crew` in steps of size `size`, creating and pushing chunks from `crew` into `chunks` using `slice()`

- return the `chunks` array

hints.text: You should create an empty array named `chunks`.
You should use a `for` loop to build chunks.
hints.test:
const cleaned = __helpers.removeWhiteSpace(__helpers.removeJSComments(chunkCrew.toString()));
assert.match(cleaned, /for\s*\(/);

hints.text: Inside the `for` loop, you should call `push()` on the `chunks` array to insert every sliced chunk (which must be created by calling `slice()` on the `crew` array).
hints.test:
const cleaned = __helpers.removeWhiteSpace(__helpers.removeJSComments(chunkCrew.toString()));
assert.match(cleaned, /chunks\.push\(crew\.slice\(/);

hints.text: After the loop, you should return the `chunks` array.
Your `chunkCrew` function should return chunks of length `size` from the input array `crew` without mutating it.
